newsitem.title: UK: Horse Racing-Addington Boy out of Gold Cup, wait on Coome Hill.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Addington Boy out of Gold Cup, wait on Coome Hill.

text.p: Addington Boy will not run in the Grade One Gold Cup Chase at Cheltenham because of a leg injury, trainer Gordon Richards said on Thursday.
Richards said there had been heat in one of the horse's legs and added that Addington Boy was not fully fit.
Coome Hill (6-1) could be another non-runner after trainer Walter Dennis said on television on Thursday morning that the going at Prestbury Park may be too fast for his stable star.
Dennis said he would have to sit down with his family to discuss the situation before a final decision is made.
Philip Arkwright, clerk of the course at Cheltenham, said the course had not dried out to any degree and he added that it will ride fast but good.
"I think the race will be fast-run as there is no soft ground stopping them and that is as it should be," Arkwright said.
There were fears that leading Irish novice Dorans Pride (8- 1) would also be withdrawn by trainer Michael Hourigan because of the fast ground.
But Hourigan walked the course on Thursday morning and said at 1130 GMT that his stable star will take his chance.
"If not this year, he'll be back next year. I'm confident about a good run, but his chance is another thing. But if we're not in we can't win," Hourigan said.
"He'll run a big race if he can go the gallop for the first two miles. I ran Deep Bramble here in this race before and he was off the bridle all the way, but this is a better horse.
"We'll drop him in and see how he carries Shane (Broderick, the jockey) and if he carries him well on the first circuit, I think he'll be okay," he added.

Irish-trained entries were to the fore in the betting for the three miles and two furlong (4.2-km) contest on Thursday with 1996 Gold Cup champion Imperial Call a 5-1 chance and both and Danoli quoted at 7-1.
